faqs.q: What is a blank invoice template?
faqs.a: A blank invoice template is a ready-to-fill invoice layout — header, bill-to block, line-item table, tax and total rows — with all content fields left empty. You add your business details and the job's charges each time, on paper or on screen.

faqs.q: Can I download a blank invoice in Excel?
faqs.a: Yes. The free Excel version keeps the formulas: type quantities and rates and the subtotal, tax and total recalculate automatically. The Word and PDF versions are blank layouts you type into or print.

faqs.q: Can I print blank invoices and fill them in by hand?
faqs.a: Yes. The PDF version prints a clean invoice sheet with empty rows — many trades keep a stack in the van and write invoices on site, then enter them into the spreadsheet later.
Yes. The PDF, Word and Excel versions are free with no email required and no watermark.

deepDive.heading: Using blank invoices correctly: numbering, tax rows and record-keeping
deepDive.sub: A blank invoice is only as good as the habits around it — here is how sole traders and small shops fill them in so they hold up at tax time and in payment disputes.

paras: A blank invoice tempts you into the one habit that causes trouble later: issuing invoices with no number, or restarting numbering every month. Bookkeepers and courts treat an unnumbered invoice as an informal note, not a bill — and if a client disputes payment, your numbering sequence is the evidence that the document was issued, when, and in what order. Start at 1001 or 0001 and increment every invoice by one, whether it is printed, typed or spreadsheet-generated.

The Excel version of this template numbers itself if you keep one file per client and save-as per job — 1024-save becomes 1025, and the paper stack in the van stays in the same sequence. Skip codes, keep the sequence: 1004, 1005, 1006. Gaps invite questions; restarts break your own audit trail.

blocks.h3: The tax row: fill it only when your state taxes what you sold
paras: The tax rate cell is blank on purpose, because what goes in it depends on what you sold and where. Most states tax tangible goods but not labor-only services; some tax services tied to goods (a repair with parts), and a handful tax most services outright. Washington, New Mexico and Hawaii tax broadly; most others do not. If you invoice only labor in a state that does not tax labor, the correct entry in the tax row is nothing at all — leave it empty and the total equals the subtotal.

The line-level taxable flag in this template exists for the mixed case: mark the parts rows taxable and the labor rows exempt, enter your combined state + local rate once, and the formula applies tax to the right lines only. That single distinction — which rows carry tax — is the most common error on hand-filled invoices, and it is the one state auditors look for first.

blocks.h3: Handwritten invoices are legal — if the record survives
paras: A blank invoice you print and fill in with a pen is a perfectly valid commercial document in every U.S. state. What matters is what happens after the client takes their copy: the copy you keep must survive until tax season and beyond. The working patterns that last:
list: Carbonless duplicate pads (2- or 3-part NCR paper): the client gets the top sheet, you keep the yellow copy in the truck, and the pink copy files at the office. No scanner needed.
Photograph-and-file: snap the signed invoice before leaving the driveway, and file the photo by client name and date. At year end the photo folder is your revenue ledger.

Type-in-later: hand-write on site, then transcribe into the Excel version that evening. The typed file becomes the record; the paper is the source document. This is the pattern most solo trades land on eventually.

blocks.h3: What a client's bookkeeper looks for (and routes to the bottom of the pile)
paras: Accounts-payable clerks process hundreds of invoices a week, and the ones that get paid on the next check run share the same four traits: a sequential invoice number, a clear due date, payment terms written on the document, and a total that matches the agreed quote. An invoice missing any of these waits for a phone call, and the phone call waits for the clerk's mood.

This blank layout ships with all four fields positioned where AP software and human clerks expect to scan for them: number and date at the top right, terms and due date directly under the table, total at the bottom right. Fill them every time, even on the handwritten copies, and blank invoices stop being a payment-risk format.

blocks.h3: Year-end: your blank invoices are your revenue record
paras: For sole proprietors and single-member LLCs, the invoice file is the primary evidence of gross receipts — Schedule C starts from what you invoiced, not what the bank deposited, when the two differ (deposits lag, checks bounce, cash gets spent). The record-keeping standard that satisfies an IRS inquiry is contemporaneous and complete: every invoice numbered, dated, and reconcilable to the sum your tax return claims.

Keep the files for at least three years after filing — six if anything is questionable, longer on the paper copies involving property work. The blank-invoice workflow that survives this is unglamorous: one folder per tax year, invoices entered in number order, and a running total that matches the return. Nothing about a blank template prevents that; everything about weekly filing habits makes it easy.

overrides.howToUseText: Use this blank invoice template whenever you need a clean, empty invoice to fill in — by hand on a clipboard, by typing in Word, or in Excel where the totals still calculate. Open the file and replace the placeholder business name and address with your own; every field below is deliberately blank, so there is no sample text to delete before you can use it. Type or write each service or product on its own line with a quantity, unit and rate — the Excel version multiplies them and updates the subtotal, tax and total as you go. If you charge sales tax, enter your state rate in the tax cell; if not, leave it blank and the total equals the subtotal. Add your payment terms and due date, then print or email the finished bill. Keep a copy per client so you have a record of what you charged and when.

howToUseSteps.title: Fill in your business details
howToUseSteps.body: Type your business name, address, phone and email at the top — or stamp the printed copy. Everything below is blank, ready for this job's details.

howToUseSteps.title: Write one line per item
howToUseSteps.body: Each row takes a description, quantity, unit and rate. The Excel version multiplies them and recalculates the subtotal, tax and total as you type.

howToUseSteps.title: Set terms and send
howToUseSteps.body: Add your payment terms and due date, then email the invoice as a PDF or hand over a printed copy. Keep one for your records.

overrides.billingText: A blank invoice is the most flexible bill format you can keep in the truck — but it pays to know when a pre-filled template is the faster choice. If you invoice the same services week after week, a template pre-filled with your line items saves typing and cuts mistakes. If every job is different — odd jobs, one-off repairs, mixed goods and services — a blank invoice keeps the sheet honest: one line per item, a quantity and a rate, and a total at the bottom. Whatever you fill in, keep three habits that get blank invoices paid. Always include an invoice number and date — clients' bookkeepers route unnamed bills to the bottom of the pile. State the payment terms on the invoice itself rather than verbally. And charge sales tax only on what your state actually taxes — many states exempt services while taxing goods, and the rate cell in the Excel version is left blank on purpose so you only fill it when required. File every copy you send; come tax season, your blank invoices are your revenue record.
